earlier_scan.source_named: Nearly extinct Negros Ata (Philippines); nothing beyond wordlist/survey mentions located; no phonology or grammar found.

sources.citation: Kaufman, Daniel & Nikolaus Himmelmann. Suprasegmental phonology (Philippine/W Austronesian overview chapter); Zorc, R. David 1993. Overview of Austronesian and Philippine accent patterns; Zorc field-note archive menu (SEAlang).
sources.note: No entry for Negros Ata / Inata in any of them; Zorc's field-note archive has no Ata (Negros) list.

sources.citation: Bunnie, Marcelo (collector). 1973. 'Ata - Negrito dialect'. Expanded Philippine Word List (1966 master list), taken at Cangguhob, Mabinay, Negros Oriental, November 1973. Handwritten original, 10 pp. SIL International - Philippines, Collection of Unpublished Materials.
sources.note: Word list only; key '? - question mark is glottal stop'. A handful of items carry sporadic diacritics (grave/acute-like marks, asterisk over vowel before final glottal stop) but there is no systematic stress marking and no note on stress.
Stub; sole source cited is Lobel 2013 p.85; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (revised ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. (chapter on language names)
sources.note: Mentions 'Inati of Panay Island and Inata of Negros Island' only as reflexes of PMP *qaRta (name etymology); no linguistic data.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: Issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. xx+422 pp. (section 3.2.7 'Ata', pp.85-86; Table of Black Filipino groups pp.62-63; p.55)
sources.note: Nothing on Inata phonology or stress. p.85: only 3-4 elderly rememberers, data inconsistent between and within speakers, 'it is impossible at present to make any reliable analysis of the Inata language'; p.86 'we may never know the truth about the Inata language'.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1994. Possible Non-Austronesian lexical elements in Philippine Negrito languages. Oceanic Linguistics 33(1): 37-72.
sources.note: Negros Ata is not among the languages with data (only Ata Manobo appears); nothing on stress for this language.

sources.citation: Same word list, typed carbon copy, 9 pp.: header 'Taken from - Cangguhob, Mebinay, Neg. Or., Negros / By - Marcelo Bunnie / Ata - Negrito dialect / November 1973'; key '? = glottal stop, e = [wedge]'. SIL Philippines unpublished materials.
sources.note: Typed forms carry no stress marks; no phonology note.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 2013. Who are the Philippine Negritos? Evidence from language. Human Biology 85(1), Article 15.

sources.note: Overview of Negrito languages that may summarize what (if anything) is known of Inata from Lobel's data; would confirm absence of description rather than supply a stress rule.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason W. Unpublished Inata field data (elicitation with 2-4 elderly rememberers, northern Negros and Mabinay/Bais area, 2005-2007), referenced in Lobel 2013:62-63, 85-86.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only modern linguist-collected Inata material; if any transcription marks stress it would be here. Lobel himself judges the data too inconsistent for analysis, so expectations are low.
